summary: A description of a TENEX subsystem called SMFS for working with UCSB's Simple-Minded File System. It lets TENEX users store, retrieve, delete and rename files at UCSB. Files can be protected, and a file stored from one TENEX system can be retrieved from another.

plainLanguage.summary: A program that lets people keep files in a remote locker at another school. You can put in, take out and rename things from your own computer.

subtitle: TENEX subsystem for accessing UCSB's remote file storage

tldr.problem: TENEX users at remote sites needed a way to store files at UCSB's Simple-Minded File System and manage them without learning a completely new interface.
tldr.mechanism: The SMFS subsystem lets TENEX users transparently transfer, delete, rename and protect files at UCSB through familiar TENEX commands. Files can be cross-host portable: stored from one TENEX system and retrieved from another.
tldr.outcome: Network users could use UCSB's on-line storage as an archive with protection and cross-system portability through a familiar interface.

today: RFC 409 is classified as Unknown status. It documented a specific TENEX file management tool for accessing UCSB's Simple-Minded File System.

sections.title: SMFS Subsystem Overview
sections.content: The Simple-Minded File System (SMFS) is a TENEX subsystem that interfaces ARPANET TENEX users to UCSB-MOD75's remote file storage system. SMFS manages approximately 10K pages of on-line, direct-access storage at UCSB. Using SMFS, users can transfer files to and from UCSB, and delete and rename them while they reside at Santa Barbara. Files can be read and/or write protected, and a file stored to UCSB from one TENEX system can be retrieved from another, providing cross-system portability.
sections.plainLanguage: SMFS is a subsystem that lets TENEX computers talk to UCSB's file storage. You can copy files there, protect them, and another TENEX computer can get them back.

sections.title: Capabilities and Limitations
sections.content: The subsystem is installed at SRI-ARC. SMFS can archive most files from a TENEX file system, but it cannot handle long files (in the strict TENEX sense) or files whose directory name, filename, or extension contains non-alphanumeric characters, or whose combined length exceeds 32 characters. These naming restrictions arise from limitations at UCSB. Files can be protected with read and write restrictions, and the cross-host portability means files are not locked to a single system.
sections.plainLanguage: SMFS can store most files, but not super-long ones or files with weird characters in the name. You can lock files so others cannot read or change them.

sections.title: Command Interface
sections.content: SMFS is invoked like any other TENEX subsystem by typing its name. It responds with a herald showing the version and date, then prompts the user with '#'. Users enter commands by typing the first letter; SMFS acknowledges recognition by completing the keyword. Commands requiring arguments prompt for each one in turn, with keywords listed as alternatives. Character editing features are available: control-A deletes the previous character, control-X deletes the entire string, and control-R retypes it. For filenames, control-W deletes the current field, control-F recognizes it, and ESC recognizes all remaining fields.
sections.plainLanguage: You start the program and type commands. It shows you what you typed to confirm it understands. You can edit what you type with special keys.

references.text: Pickens, J., "UCSB Simple File System", RFC 399, 1972.
